name: Emission-Absorption Model
definition: The most widely used optical rendering model for volume rendering, taking into account both light emission and absorption in the volume. It solves the problem of calculating final radiance reaching the camera from a participating medium.
summary: The Emission-Absorption Model is the standard direct volume rendering technique that computes radiance by integrating emitted light attenuated by absorption, distinguishing it from emission-only models by accounting for occlusion and from full radiative transfer models by ignoring scattering.
